Across its 63 WLC occurrences Hebrew עצר means restrain, detain, imprison, shut (womb, heavens) and, as עֲצָרָה/עֲצֶרֶת, a (closing) assembly; it never means pressing out juice and never names a time of day. It therefore matches the Arabic habs/alıkoyma branch (paras 11, 14) and inverts the pressed-cloud image (para 8: the held heavens give no rain). The Joseph cupbearer scene uses the hapax שׂחט, not עצר. An Aramaic עצר 'press' in Targum Onkelos is proposed from memory only.

Sound correspondence only. Hebrew צבר (8 WLC occurrences) means only 'heap up' (Gen 41:35, 41:49 Joseph's grain; Ps 39:7 futile heaping; Job 27:16, Zech 9:3 silver like dust; Exod 8:10 frogs; Hab 1:10 dust; 2 Kgs 10:8 heaps). Neither patience nor the bitter aloe juice of para 10 is attested; the block at para 13 marks it as same consonants with a different sense, not as wordplay or evidence of relation.
